'''Stephen Kresovich''' (born 1952)<ref name="thesis">{{Cite journal|url=https://library.ohio-state.edu/record=b8120234~S7|title=The potential of sorghum as a raw material for ethanol production in midwestern cropping systems|first=Stephen|last=Kresovich|date=April 27, 1982|journal=Dissertation Abstracts International|pages=43–05|via=library.ohio-state.edu Library Catalog}}</ref> is a plant geneticist and the [https://www.clemson.edu/cafls/research/endowed-chair/index.html Coker Endowed Chair of Genetics] in the [https://www.clemson.edu/cafls/departments/plant-environmental-sciences/ Department of Plant and Environmental Sciences] at [[Clemson University]]<ref name="facultypage">{{Cite web|title=Employee Profiles {{!}} College of Agriculture, Forestry and Life Sciences {{!}} Clemson University, South Carolina|url=https://www.clemson.edu/cafls/faculty_staff/profiles/skresov|access-date=2021-03-24|website=www.clemson.edu}}</ref> and professor in the [https://cals.cornell.edu/school-integrative-plant-science School of Integrative Plant Science] in the [https://cals.cornell.edu/ College of Agriculture and Life Sciences] at [[Cornell University]]. Since 2019 he has served as director of the [https://web.archive.org/web/20200811213926/https://ilci.cornell.edu/ Feed the Future Innovation Lab for Crop Improvement].

== Education ==

Kresovich received an A.B. in Biology in 1974 from [[Washington and Jefferson College]], an M.S. in Agronomy from [[Texas A&M University]] in 1977, and his PhD from [[Ohio State University|Ohio State]] in 1982.

== Career and Research ==
Kresovich has worked at Clemson University since 2013 as the Robert and Lois Coker Trustees Chair of Genetics and [http://sfntoday.com/sorghum-geneticist-to-lead-clemson-research/ director] of the [https://www.clemson.edu/centers-institutes/itg/departments/apt/ Advanced Plant Technology Program], integrating advances in genetics and genomics to solve problems in agriculture, the environment, and human health. Kresovich held numerous administrative appointments at Cornell University from 1998-2009,<ref>{{Cite web|title=Plant geneticist Stephen Kresovich to head Cornell's Institute for Biotechnology and Life Science Technologies|url=https://news.cornell.edu/stories/2000/11/plant-geneticist-stephen-kresovich-head-institute-biotechnology-and-life-science|access-date=2021-03-24|website=Cornell Chronicle|language=en}}</ref> including Vice Provost for Life Sciences from 2005-2009.<ref>{{Cite web|date=April 26, 2005|title=Two new vice provosts, Moody-Adams and Kresovich, are announced at Cornell|url=https://news.cornell.edu/stories/2005/04/two-new-vice-provosts-moody-adams-and-kresovich-are-announced|access-date=2021-03-24|website=Cornell Chronicle|language=en}}</ref> He played a key role in the conception and launch of Weill Hall,<ref>{{Cite news |last=Ramanujan |first=Krishna |title=Cornell University |url=https://news.cornell.edu/stories/2008/10/weill-hall-center-ideas-innovation-collaboration |work=Cornell Chronicle}}</ref> a life sciences research center on Cornell's main campus. Kresovich re-established his connection with Cornell University in 2019 as director of the [[United States Agency for International Development|USAID]] Feed the Future Innovation Lab for Crop Improvement,<ref>{{Cite web|title=Crop-improvement lab established with $25M USAID grant|url=https://news.cornell.edu/stories/2019/10/crop-improvement-lab-established-25m-usaid-grant|access-date=2021-03-24|website=Cornell Chronicle|language=en}}</ref> and in 2020, was appointed a member of the National Genetic Resources Advisory Council by the [[United States Secretary of Agriculture|U.S. Secretary of Agriculture]].<ref>{{Cite web|date=2020-04-28|title=Clemson plant geneticist appointed to National Genetic Resources Advisory Council · Clemson News|url=https://news.clemson.edu/clemson-plant-geneticist-appointed-to-national-genetic-resources-advisory-council/|access-date=2021-03-26|website=Clemson News|language=en-US}}</ref>

From 2009-2011, Kresovich served as the Vice President for Research and Graduate Education at the [[University of South Carolina]]<ref>{{Cite web|title=Stephen Kresovich heads to University of South Carolina|url=https://news.cornell.edu/stories/2009/07/kresovich-head-university-south-carolina|access-date=2021-03-24|website=Cornell Chronicle|language=en}}</ref> and [https://sc.edu/about/offices_and_divisions/research/centersandfacilities/smart_state/smartstatechairs.php South Carolina SmartState Endowed Chair] until 2013. Prior to joining the Cornell faculty in 1998, Kresovich served as an agronomist at the [[Battelle Memorial Institute]] in 1977<ref name="DOEEI">Energy Insider, 1978, Department of Energy, Page 59.</ref> and for eleven years as Laboratory Director at two [https://www.ars-grin.gov/Pages/Collections U.S. National Genetic Resources Program genebanks] in [[Geneva, New York]] (1987–93) and [[Griffin, Georgia]] (1993-98).

Kresovich’s research focuses on conservation genetics and improvement of crop plants including sorghum, maize, and sugar cane. His research objectives have included: (1) to identify genes of the sorghum, sugar cane, and maize genomes impacting evolution, domestication or crop improvement, (2) to characterize and understand the relationship between DNA sequence variation and desirable phenotypes, (3) to characterize molecular and phenotypic diversity of sorghum, sugar cane, and maize in natural populations, landraces, and elite germplasm, and (4) to develop and test strategies to efficiently discover, conserve, and use variation in natural populations and genebank collections by integrating current advances in genomics, bioinformatics, and plant genetics/breeding.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Research {{!}} Kresovich Program|url=https://www.skgenomics.com/research|access-date=2021-03-24|website=skgenomics|language=en}}</ref>

{{cite journal
| last = Coyne
| first = Dermot P
| date = 1997
| title = Fellows of the Crop Science Society of America
| url = https://acsess.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.2135/cropsci1997.0011183X003700020072x
| journal = Crop Science
| volume = 37
| issue = 2
| pages = 663–670
| doi = 10.2135/cropsci1997.0011183X003700020072x
| s2cid = 252149126
| access-date = 
| url-access = subscription

He has been awarded outstanding manuscript on “Plant Genetic Resources” in Crop Science in 2002,<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Gethi|first1=James G.|last2=Labate|first2=Joanne A.|last3=Lamkey|first3=Kendall R.|last4=Smith|first4=Margaret E.|last5=Kresovich|first5=Stephen|date=May 2002|title=SSR Variation in Important U.S. Maize Inbred Lines|url=http://dx.doi.org/10.2135/cropsci2002.9510|journal=Crop Science|volume=42|issue=3|pages=951–957|doi=10.2135/cropsci2002.9510|issn=0011-183X|url-access=subscription}}</ref> 2006,<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Rice|first1=Elizabeth B.|last2=Smith|first2=Margaret E.|last3=Mitchell|first3=Sharon E.|last4=Kresovich|first4=Stephen|date=January 2006|title=Conservation and Change: A Comparison of In situ and Ex situ Conservation of Jala Maize Germplasm|url=http://dx.doi.org/10.2135/cropsci2005.06-0116|journal=Crop Science|volume=46|issue=1|pages=428–436|doi=10.2135/cropsci2005.06-0116|issn=0011-183X|url-access=subscription}}</ref> and 2011.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Brown|first1=Patrick J.|last2=Myles|first2=Sean|last3=Kresovich|first3=Stephen|date=January 2011|title=Genetic Support for Phenotype-based Racial Classification in Sorghum|url=http://dx.doi.org/10.2135/cropsci2010.03.0179|journal=Crop Science|volume=51|issue=1|pages=224–230|doi=10.2135/cropsci2010.03.0179|issn=0011-183X|url-access=subscription}}</ref> Kresovich has also received certificates of Merit from the [[United States Department of Agriculture|U.S. Department of Agriculture]], [[Agricultural Research Service]] from 1989-1991 and 1995-1997, as well as a research award from the International Vetiver Research Network (World Bank and King of Thailand) in 1993.
